body.translated_text: The Noble <s>Advayaśatikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra</s> (The Noble Perfection of Wisdom in One Hundred Non-Dual [Verses])
Homage to the blessed noble <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom)!

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam / ekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharatisma gṛdhrakūṭe parvate mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhamardhatrayodaśabhirbhikṣuśatairanekairbrahmaśakralokapālairdevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragarūḍakinnaramahoragairūpāsakopāsikābhiḥ sārdham /
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain, together with a great assembly of monks — three hundred and fifty monks — along with many <s>Brahmas</s>, <s>Śakras</s>, world-guardians (<s>lokapālas</s>), gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, <s>upāsakas</s> (male lay devotees), and <s>upāsikās</s> (female lay devotees).

body.text: tatra khalu bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtiṃmāmantrayate sma / ye kecit subhūte śrāvakamārgaḥ śikṣitukāmena prajñāpāramitā śrotavyā udgṛhītavyā dhārayitavyā vācayitavyādeśayitavyā paryavāptavyā / ihaiva prajñāpāramitāyāmupāyakauśalya samanvāgatena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena sarvabuddhadharmasamudāgamāya yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? iha prajñāpāramitāyāṃ vistareṇa sarvabuddhadharmā nirdiṣṭāḥ / yatra bodhisattvena śikṣitavyam, ye kecit subhūte kuśaladharmā bodhipakṣāḥ śrāvakadharmā vā pratyeka buddhadharmā vā bodhisatvadharmā vā buddhadharmā vā / bodhipakṣāḥ śrāvakadharmāḥ pratyekabuddhadharmā bodhisatvadharmāstvaṃ te prajñāpāramitāyāmantargatāmanupraviṣṭāḥ saṃgrahasamavasaraṇaṃ gacchanti / bhagavānāha - tadyathā subhūte dānapāramiutā śīlapāramitā kṣāntipāramitā vīryapāramitā dhyānapāramitā prajñāpāramitā / adhyātmaśūnyatā vahirdhāśūnyatā adhyātmavahirdhāśūnyatā śūnyatā śūnyatā mahāśūnyatā paramārthaśūnyatā saṃskṛtaśūnyatā asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā atyanta śūnyatā anavarāgraśūnyatā anavakāraśūnyatā prakṛtiśūnyatā sarvadharmaśūnyatā svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā anupalambhaśūnyatā abhāvaśūnyatā svabhāvaśūnyatā abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā / catvāri smṛutyupasthānāni / catvāri samyakprahāṇāni / catvāri ṛddhipādāni / pañcendriyāṇi / pañcabalāni / saptabodhyaṅgāni / āryāṣṭāṅgikamārgāḥ // catvāri dhyānāni / catvāri pramāṇāni / catasra ārūpyasamāpattayaḥ / aṣṭau vimokṣāḥ / navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ / sarvadhāraṇīmukhāni / daśatathāgatabalāni / catvāri vaiśāradyāni / catasraḥ pratisaṃvidaḥ / mahamaitrī mahākarūṇā / aṣṭādaśāveṇikabuddhadharmāḥ śrotāpattiphalaṃ sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ anāgāmiphalaṃ sarvajñatā ca //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'Whosoever, O <s>Subhūti</s>, wishes to train in the path of a <s>śrāvaka</s> (disciple) should hear, take up, retain, recite, teach, and master the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. A <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> endowed with skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>) in this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should apply effort (<s>yoga</s>) for the attainment of all the <s>buddhadharmas</s>. Why is that? Because in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> all the <s>buddhadharmas</s> are set forth in detail. Here the <s>bodhisattva</s> should train; whatever wholesome dharmas (<s>kuśaladharmā</s>) there are — aids to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>), dharmas of the <s>śrāvaka</s>, dharmas of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, dharmas of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, or dharmas of the <s>Buddha</s> — all of these are included in, have entered into, and converge upon the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: That is to say, O <s>Subhūti</s>: the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving), the <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of ethics), the <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience), the <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of energy), the <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation), the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom); <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> (inner emptiness), <s>bāhirdhāśūnyatā</s> (outer emptiness), <s>adhyātmabāhirdhāśūnyatā</s> (inner-and-outer emptiness), <s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of emptiness), <s>mahāśūnyatā</s> (great emptiness), <s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s> (ultimate emptiness), <s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the conditioned), <s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the unconditioned), <s>atyantaśūnyatā</s> (absolute emptiness), <s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of what has no beginning or end), <s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of what is not to be discarded), <s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of inherent nature), <s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of all dharmas), <s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of own-characteristics), <s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-apprehension), <s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-existence), <s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of self-nature), <s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence); the four <s>smṛtyupasthānāni</s> (establishments of mindfulness); the four <s>samyakprahāṇāni</s> (right efforts); the four <s>ṛddhipādāni</s> (bases of miraculous power); the five <s>indriyas</s> (faculties); the five <s>balas</s> (powers); the seven <s>bodhyaṅgāni</s> (factors of awakening); the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgikamārga</s>); the four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions); the four <s>pramāṇas</s> (immeasurables); the four <s>ārūpyasamāpattis</s> (formless attainments); the eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations); the nine progressive meditative attainments (<s>navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>); all <s>dhāraṇīmukhas</s> (entrances to <s>dhāraṇī</s>); the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>daśatathāgatabalāni</s>); the four fearlessnesses (<s>catvāri vaiśāradyāni</s>); the four analytical knowledges (<s>catasraḥ pratisaṃvidaḥ</s>); great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>); great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>); the eighteen exclusive dharmas of the Buddha (<s>aṣṭādaśāveṇikabuddhadharmāḥ</s>); the fruit of stream-entry (<s>śrotāpattiphala</s>), the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>), the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>), and omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>).

body.text: iyameva subhūte kuśaladharmā bodhipakṣāḥ śrāvakadharmāḥ pratyekabuddhadharmāḥ / yatra prajñāpāramitāyāmantargatā anupraviṣṭāḥ sagrahasamavasaraṇaṃ gacchanti /
body.translated_text: These, O <s>Subhūti</s>, are precisely the wholesome dharmas, the aids to awakening, the dharmas of the <s>śrāvaka</s>, the dharmas of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> — all are included in, have entered into, and converge upon the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: subhūtirāha - aho! aho!duravagāhā vateyaṃ prajñāpāramitā / yatra hi nāma kuśaladharmā bodhipakṣāḥ śrāvakadharmāḥ pratyekabuddhadharmā bodhisatvadharmā buddhadharmā iti / yato prajñāpāramitāyāmantargatā anupraviṣṭāḥ saṃgrahasamavasaraṇaṃ gacchanti /
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'Ah! Ah! How truly deep is this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>! Indeed, the wholesome dharmas — aids to awakening, dharmas of the <s>śrāvaka</s>, dharmas of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, dharmas of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, dharmas of the <s>Buddha</s> — all are included in, have entered into, and converge upon the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.'
The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Because of its absolute freedom (<s>atyantamuktatva</s>), O <s>Subhūti</s>, [is] the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.'
<s>Subhūti</s> said: 'Ah! Ah! How truly deep is this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>!'
The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Because of its utter purity (<s>atyantaviśuddhatva</s>), O <s>Subhūti</s>, [is] the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.'

body.text: subhūtirāha - aho! aho! duravagāhā vateyaṃ bhagavan prajñāpāramitā /
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'Ah! Ah! How truly deep, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>!'

body.text: bhagavānāha - atyantaśuddhatvāt subhūte prajñāpāramitā, tasmāttarhi subhūte ākāśopamā prajñāpāramitā /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Because of its absolute purity (<s>atyantaśuddhatva</s>), O <s>Subhūti</s>, [is] the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; therefore, O <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is comparable to space (<s>ākāśopamā</s>).'

body.text: subhūtirāha - aho! aho! duravagāhā vateya prajñāpāramitā bhagavan abhiyuktena /
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'Ah! Ah! How truly deep, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, [even] for one who is diligent!'

body.text: bhagavānāha - evameva tadyathā vadasi / duradhimocā prajñāpāramitā anabhiyuktena parītakuśalamūlena durmedhasa anāvilena subhūtinā / nahi na yadyena pāpamitrasahitena pāpamitrasavargeṇa bahulena pāpamitrasamādāyena saddharmāntaka samanvāgatena ādikarmikeṇa atyantarūpeṇa aparipṛcchakajātīyena duṣprajñasaṃvarttanīyena kusīdena hīnasatvena nādhimuktena kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu anabhiyuktena tasyaiva hi subhūte duradhimocāṃ prajñāpāramitāmucyate /
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Just so — it is as you say. The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) is hard to comprehend, O <s>Subhūti</s>, for one who is not diligent, who has meager roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>), who is of dull intellect, who is impure. Indeed, it is for such a one — one who keeps company with bad friends, who belongs to the class of bad friends, who is heavily attended by bad friends, who is endowed with the destruction of the true <s>Dharma</s>, who is a mere beginner (<s>ādikarmika</s>), who is of extremely limited nature, who is of the type that does not inquire, who tends toward bad wisdom, who is lazy, who is a being of low aspiration, who has no faith, who is not devoted to wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — indeed, O <s>Subhūti</s>, for that very one the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is called 'hard to comprehend.'"

body.text: punaraparaṃ subhūte yaḥ kaścit kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāṃ prajñāpāramitāṃ gambhīrāṃ bhāṣanti dhārayi vācayi deśayi paryavāpsyanti so 'tītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ bhagavatāṃ buddhabodhiṃ bodhisattvā dhārayiṣyanti / tasmāttarhi subhūte adhyāśayena bhikṣavo 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhikāmenābhijñyaprajñāpāramitā udgṛhītavyā /
body.translated_text: "Furthermore, O <s>Subhūti</s>, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family speaks, upholds, recites, teaches, and fully comprehends this profound <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> will uphold the <s>Buddha</s>-awakening (<s>buddhabodhi</s>) of the Blessed Ones of the past, future, and present. Therefore, O <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be taken up by monks with superior aspiration (<s>adhyāśaya</s>), desiring unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), having realized it through direct knowledge (<s>abhijñā</s>)."

body.text: idamavocad bhagavānnāttamanā sā ca sarvāvatī parvadīyaṃ bhagavato bhāṣitamabhinandanniti //
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One. Delighted, the entire assembly rejoiced in what the Blessed One had spoken.
The <s>Advayaśatikā Prajñāpāramitā Dhāraṇī Sūtra</s> (The Sūtra-Dhāraṇī of the Perfection of Wisdom in Two Hundred [Verses] on Non-Duality) is completed.
